opps.title: 3 accounts stopped ordering — $1,284 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, Turf and Barrel, was worth 991 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

rows.label: Turf and Barrel
rows.detail: On Premise · North Arlington · 991 cases in 2025

opps.title: Coors Light — 11% of your commission, down 9% YoY
opps.body: Sales are down 1,210 cases (9%) vs last year, but Coors Light is still 10.7% of your total commission — your #3 brand. That decline has already cost about $1,210 in modeled commission, and recovering half of it is worth roughly $605. On a brand this size that is a bigger swing than anything you could realistically open new this year. 149 accounts bought it last year; 146 have this year — 3 accounts stopped carrying it.

opps.title: 8 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 559 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 559 cases and about $559 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.

The drop is concentrated in Modelo Especial (-167 cases), Lite (-124 cases) — a mix problem you can work on the next visit, not a lost account.
